name: DOVER Corp
moat_justification: Moderate/narrow (5/10). Dover holds leading niche positions across five diversified industrial segments with real installed-base, aftermarket and consumables pull-through, a pricing/productivity record, and disciplined bolt-on M&A compounding. But the advantages are local to each niche: no network effects, no portfolio-wide structural cost advantage, credible well-resourced rivals in every segment, and end-markets tied to cyclical industrial capex — revenue CAGR was only 1.04% over 3 years and 3.90% over 5 years. That is a collection of narrow moats, not a wide one. CAP = 8.5 years.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 9 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2024 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base
one_liner: Quality diversified industrial compounder, moat 5/10, but at $193.33 it does not clear 15% — weighted IRR 7.97%, weighted IV@15% $81.97; it would need a price at or below $81.97 to clear the hurdle on the weighted case.
moat_for: Leading niche positions across five diversified industrial segments
Installed-base, aftermarket and consumables pull-through (marking/coding, pumps, fueling, refrigeration)
Pricing/productivity record — Q2 2026 total segment earnings margin 24.0%
Disciplined bolt-on M&A compounding and a long record of consecutive dividend increases
moat_against: No network effects; engineered components face credible rivals in every segment
Cyclical industrial-capex end markets — revenue CAGR 1.04% (3y) / 3.90% (5y)
Pricing power is modest and segment-specific, not portfolio-wide
Conglomerate structure — advantages are local, not structural at group level
